headline: Buybacks drive EPS surge as underlying margins normalize
summary_short: Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 2.2% y/y to $9.79B and diluted EPS jumped 16.9% to $11.54, but the EPS surge was driven far more by a 13.1% y/y cut in diluted share count from buybacks than by profit growth — net income attributable to Lithia rose just 1.5% y/y to $260.0M.
summary_long: Revenue grew 2.2% y/y to $9.79B on used-vehicle and aftersales volume from acquisitions; same-store revenue fell 1.6%. Gross profit rose only 0.8% y/y as same-store new-vehicle margin normalized (-80bps) and F&I softened (-5.2% same-store), partly offset by aftersales margin gains (+120bps) and a stronger Financing Operations segment (interest margin 4.8% vs 4.5%). Operating margin expanded 20bps on a lower SG&A ratio and better Financing Operations profitability. Net income attributable to Lithia rose just 1.5% y/y to $260.0M, but diluted EPS jumped 16.9% to $11.54 as diluted shares fell 13.1% y/y on $534.0M of H1 buybacks (Board added a $500M authorization in May, total $3.7B). Cash fell to $110.3M from $202.8M y/y; equity fell 8.4% y/y. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by increases in used-vehicle and aftersales volume related to acquisitions; same-store new-vehicle revenue fell 1.5% on a 2.2% unit-volume decline, partially offset by a 0.1% rise in average selling price.

Total gross profit grew on acquisition growth and same-store aftersales gains, but same-store new-vehicle gross profit per unit fell 11.1% on an 80bps margin decline from continued margin normalization.
Operating margin rose 20bps, primarily due to decreased SG&A as a percentage of revenue and improved profitability of the Financing Operations segment.

Net income growth was comparatively small; the filing attributes the year's net income change overall to higher SG&A as a percentage of gross profit and equity-method investment losses, partly offset by revenue and gross-profit gains.
Diluted share count fell 13.1% y/y (25.9M to 22.5M) on $534.0M of buybacks in H1 2026, which arithmetically amplifies EPS growth well beyond the underlying 1.5% net income increase.

Cash declined after H1 2026 capital deployment of $534.0M in share repurchases, $221.7M in acquisitions and $153.4M in capital expenditures, funded partly through increased floor-plan and non-recourse note borrowings.

Management reiterated its standing capital-allocation target (25-35% acquisitions, 25% capex/innovation, 40-50% shareholder return) and noted it now favors repurchases over acquisitions given elevated acquisition pricing and recent share-price trends; no numeric FY2026 guidance was issued.
